**SECTION D: COMPOSITION WRITING (10 MARKS).** Write a composition of between 200-250 words on ONE of the topics below.

**Topic 1.** Last week your family organized the traditional wedding of your older sister. You were actively involved in the ceremony. You want to let your friends get a feel of what happened. Narrate what happened to them by considering the following: when and where it took place, the different stages of the ceremony, who attended and their impressions and your general impression.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
La rédaction anglaise du BAC sanctionne autant le respect du format imposé (récit narratif chronologique, lettre d'encouragement amicale, article de journal structuré en causes/conséquences/solutions) que le contenu. Un récit de cérémonie traditionnelle doit suivre l'ordre chronologique des événements décrits dans la consigne (quand, où, étapes, invités, impressions) ; une lettre d'encouragement à un ami en difficulté doit rester chaleureuse tout en couvrant chacun des conseils demandés par la consigne ; un article sur la violence scolaire doit suivre la structure imposée (causes, conséquences, solutions), jamais une seule de ces trois parties. Comme le sujet propose un choix, un seul texte doit être rédigé le jour de l'examen ; les modèles ci-dessous illustrent chacun l'un des formats possibles.

## Topic 1 - Narrative composition (modèle, environ 220 mots)

Last Saturday, my family organised the traditional wedding of my older sister, Solange, at my grandfather's compound in our home village, and I was right at the centre of the preparations.

The ceremony began early in the morning with the arrival of the groom's family, who came bearing the traditional bride price: bags of rice, cases of drinks, and an envelope that our elders inspected carefully before the negotiations even began. As the family's designated helper, I spent the morning carrying chairs, arranging tables, and making sure every guest had a place to sit under the large tent we had rented for the occasion.

Around midday, the elders from both families sat together for the formal negotiation, a mixture of serious discussion and good-humoured teasing that had everyone laughing by the end. Once the families agreed, my sister was presented, dressed in traditional attire, to loud cheers, drumming, and dancing that lasted well into the afternoon.

What struck me most was watching my grandmother's face as she watched her granddaughter being formally welcomed into another family, proud but also visibly emotional. Guests from both villages mingled freely, sharing food and stories long after the official ceremony had ended.

By evening, exhausted but happy, I realised I had just witnessed something far more meaningful than a party: a genuine joining of two families, built on respect for tradition that I hope to carry forward myself one day.

**SECTION D: COMPOSITION WRITING (10 MARKS).** Write a composition of between 200-250 words on ONE of the topics below.

**Topic 2.** When the Probatoire results were published last August, your best friend failed and has been avoiding coming close to you because you have passed. You are called Bima Rasta and your friend is called Ngong Jones. Write a letter to advise him: not to be demoralized at all because he can still make it, to join a study group with classmates, to stay away from abusive telephone usage, and to choose the subjects he is good at, etc.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 2 - Personal letter (modèle, environ 230 mots)

Dear Ngong Jones,

I have noticed you have been avoiding me since the Probatoire results came out, and I want you to know that I understand why, but I also want you to know it doesn't have to be this way between us.

Failing this exam does not define what you are capable of. Plenty of people who eventually succeeded brilliantly in life once failed an exam exactly like this one, and used it as a turning point rather than an ending. Please don't let one result convince you of something that simply isn't true about your abilities.

Here is what I honestly think could help you move forward. First, consider joining a study group with some of our classmates instead of preparing alone; explaining ideas to each other and asking questions out loud often reveals gaps that studying silently never does. Second, try to stay away from spending long hours on abusive or distracting phone calls and messages that eat into your revision time without you even noticing. Third, be honest with yourself about which subjects you are genuinely good at, and build your confidence there first before tackling your weaker areas.

Most importantly, please don't shut me out. I am not judging you, Ngong, I just want to help however I can, even if that simply means listening when things feel hard.

Take care of yourself, and let's talk soon.

Your friend,
Bima Rasta

**SECTION D: COMPOSITION WRITING (10 MARKS).** Write a composition of between 200-250 words on ONE of the topics below.

**Topic 3.** You are the Senior Prefect of your school and you have realised that violence is on the rise in your school. Write an article to be published in the "Horizon Newspaper" titled "Violence, the cankerworm in our schools today." In your article: give some of the causes of violence in school, identify some of the consequences of violence in school and suggest some possible solutions to stop this phenomenon.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 3 - Newspaper article (modèle, environ 240 mots)

**Violence, the Cankerworm in Our Schools Today**

By the Senior Prefect

Over the past few months, I have watched with growing concern as incidents of violence, verbal and physical, have become an almost normal part of daily life in our school. It is time we named this problem clearly and addressed it seriously.

Several factors feed this rise in violence. Overcrowded classrooms leave little room for teachers to notice tension before it explodes into a fight. Peer pressure pushes some students to prove themselves through aggression rather than through more constructive achievements. And for some students, difficult situations at home spill over into how they treat their classmates at school.

The consequences are serious and should worry all of us. Students who feel unsafe struggle to concentrate on their studies, some even begin avoiding school altogether. Friendships and trust between classmates break down, replaced by fear and suspicion. Left unaddressed, today's small conflicts risk becoming tomorrow's much larger problems, both inside and outside school walls.

I believe solutions exist if we commit to them together. Our school could introduce regular peer mediation sessions where students learn to resolve disputes with words rather than fists. Teachers and prefects need clearer, faster channels for reporting tension before it escalates. And parents must be brought into the conversation, since many of the pressures our students carry begin well before they reach the school gate.

Violence does not have to be the new normal in our school. But changing that will require honesty about the problem, and real commitment to the solutions, from every one of us.

### Piège à éviter
Sur ce sujet, un article qui ne développe que les causes sans jamais aborder les conséquences ni proposer de solutions, alors que la consigne demande explicitement les trois volets, perd des points même si les causes sont bien analysées.

### Conseil
Structure toujours ce type d'article en trois paragraphes clairement identifiables (causes, conséquences, solutions), avec une phrase de transition claire entre chacun : cela facilite la lecture du correcteur et montre que la consigne a été suivie point par point.

incertitudes: Le sujet propose un choix entre trois formats différents dont un seul doit être traité le jour de l'examen ; les trois modèles fournis illustrent chacun un choix possible pour couvrir l'ensemble du barème.
